prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The 2015 Conservative Manifesto sets out a long-term plan to secure a better future for hardworking people at every stage of life by putting a strong economy first, rewarding work, protecting vital public services, and upholding British values and security.

Economy and taxes
- Finish the job: eliminate the deficit, run a surplus, and keep debt falling—without raising VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance.
- Cut tax for 30 million: raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500; lift the 40p threshold to £50,000; introduce a Tax‑Free Minimum Wage law.
- Crack down on tax evasion and aggressive avoidance; maintain a competitive business tax regime; cut £10bn more red tape.

Jobs, skills and enterprise
- Create 2 million more jobs and achieve full employment.
- Deliver 3 million apprenticeships; abolish long‑term youth unemployment with a time‑limited Youth Allowance and stronger “earning or learning” requirements.
- Back small firms with a business rates review, prompt payment reforms and expanded Start Up Loans.

Welfare that makes work pay
- Lower the household benefit cap to £23,000; freeze most working‑age benefits for two years (with key exemptions); roll out Universal Credit.
- Expand free childcare to 30 hours for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds; introduce Tax‑Free Childcare.
- Encourage treatment and work for those with long‑term but treatable conditions.

Homes and ownership
- Double first‑time buyers; extend Help to Buy and launch Help to Buy ISAs.
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes at 20% discount for under‑40s; deliver 275,000 more affordable homes.
- Extend Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants; prioritise brownfield and protect the Green Belt.

NHS and care
- Keep the NHS free and funded: increase spending every year and add at least £8bn by 2020 to deliver a truly 7‑day NHS and same‑day GP access for over‑75s.
- Integrate health and social care; back mental health parity; lead on cancer, dementia, diabetes prevention; cap residential care costs.

Education and opportunity
- Guarantee a good primary place; protect per‑pupil funding; expand academies and free schools; enforce rigorous standards and core academic GCSEs.
- Boost maths, science and computing; grow University Technical Colleges; uncap university places and introduce postgraduate loans.

Security, law and order
- Complete police reform; toughen sentencing for serious crime; expand technology‑led rehabilitation.
- Support victims with a new Victims’ Law; tackle violence against women and girls.
- Replace the Human Rights Act with a British Bill of Rights.

Immigration and extremism
- Control immigration: 4‑year residency for in‑work benefits; end benefits for EU jobseekers; tougher enforcement and removals; landlord checks.
- Confront extremism with new banning and disruption orders; strengthen border security.

Infrastructure, energy and environment
- Invest over £100bn in rail, roads (including HS2/HS3), and universal superfast broadband; build the Northern Powerhouse with devolved powers and metro mayors.
- Keep bills down through competition; back new nuclear, gas and shale; halt new subsidies for onshore wind; meet climate goals cost‑effectively.
- Protect countryside and create a new marine “Blue Belt”; plant 11 million more trees.

Britain in the world and the Union
- Hold an in‑out EU referendum by end‑2017 after renegotiation; keep the pound; reclaim powers; expand free trade.
- Maintain world‑class Armed Forces, renew Trident, meet NATO commitments, and keep aid at 0.7% to tackle poverty and instability.
- Strengthen the Union: deliver new powers for Scotland and Wales; English votes for English laws; support stability in Northern Ireland.

Underlying all is a clear Conservative belief: reward those who work hard and do the right thing, protect the vulnerable, trust people and communities over bureaucracy, and keep Britain strong, secure and sovereign.
</text>
